title: Phthalate Exposure and Female Reproductive Aging
text:
This work will greatly improve our understanding about how phthalates cause early reproductive aging in
females. In turn, this work will set the foundation for the identification and development of novel targets for the
treatment of phthalate-induced diseases, including early reproductive aging.

title: Comparative analysis of DNA damage and repair capacity in dogs to improve cancer risk prediction
text:
Dogs, an important biomedical cancer model, have an increased rate of somatic mutation relative to humans,
but the mechanism driving this increase in mutation and overall cancer risk remains unknown. The goal of this
study is to test whether there are differences in (1) baseline oxidative damage and reactive oxygen species, (2)
DNA damage repair kinetics and rates of cell death; and (3) to characterize longitudinal changes in somatic
mutations in normal cells. Understanding the causes of increased rate of somatic mutation will improve the
utility of the dog as a precision cancer model and environmental sentinel, and reveal key determinants of
cancer risk.

title: Genome Editing Therapy to Treat Vision Loss in Usher Syndrome Type 2A
text:
This project aims to develop a generalized gene editing therapy for retinitis pigmentosa associated with
USH2A, the most common form of Usher Syndrome, which leads to progressive vision and hearing loss and
currently has no cure. We will employ an innovative approach to optimize gene editing strategies and delivery
methods in a clinically relevant USH2A knockout rabbit model, while also identifying biomarkers to track
disease progression and treatment efficacy. The outcomes of this research could pave the way for a novel
therapy that addresses the unmet medical needs of patients with USH2A mutations and potentially other forms
of retinitis pigmentosa.

title: Airway epithelial cell and lymphocyte interactions in chronic lung allograft dysfunction pathogenesis
text:
While lung transplantation promises improvements in survival, function, and quality of life for some end-stage
lung diseases, survival after transplantation is limited by scarring in small airways. This proposal will leverage
brushes of the small airways as a novel tool to understand how the abnormal blood supply to the transplanted
lungs could lead to inflammation and destruction of airway progenitor cells. Success in this project will improve
diagnosis of this lung scarring and allow for approaches to test treatments to prevent or reverse this disease.

title: Phthalate and bisphenol exposure in relation to infant reproductive development during minipuberty
text:
Minipuberty is a brief period in the first six months of life when infant reproductive hormones surge—in some
cases to levels nearly as high as in puberty and adulthood—and it is believed that this surge may be important
for developmental programming of the reproductive system, potentially influencing pubertal timing and future
ovarian and testicular function. This study will examine whether exposure to phthalates and bisphenols—
chemicals commonly found in plastics, food packaging, household cleaners, cosmetics, and baby products—
alters infant reproductive hormone levels and anogenital distance, an indicator of reproductive development. In
the process, using a novel method of biospecimen analysis, we will seek to identify previously unmeasured
phthalates and bisphenols that may have endocrine-disrupting properties.

title: Bioinformatics and Biostatistics Core
text: FOR CORE D The Bioinformatics and Biostatistics Core D will provide bioinformatic and biostatistical services and support data analyses for all Projects. Core D will be situated at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and led by Dr. Li Shen, who is an expert in bioinformatics and machine learning applications. One of the Core’s tasks is to support multi-omics and integrated analysis. The pre-clinical and clinical studies in Projects 1, 2, and 4 will leverage multi-omics technologies to profile systemic stress-related immune dysregulations at the cellular and molecular levels. The Core has dedicated bioinformaticians to aid PPG researchers in analyzing, visualizing, and mining data from transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics experiments in various animal models (Projects 1 and 2) and patients (Projects 2 and 4). The Core will leverage state-of-the-arts bioinformatic tools and machine learning methods for robust, efficient and integrated analyses of the multi-omics and related phenotypic data. The Core will also provide comprehensive biostatistical support. Statistical issues will be addressed at all investigatory levels, from designing experiments to interpreting results and forming conclusions. Clear distinctions will be made between conclusions based on formal hypothesis testing and important leads discovered by data exploration. Lastly, the Core aims to reduce biases, enhance reproducibility, and share data and code with the scientific community. The Core will make every effort possible to reduce potential biases in the statistical analysis. Multiple testing correction will be performed on all omics data. The Core will also share the sequencing and secondary data derived from raw images to the public. Software tools developed by the Core will also be shared as open-source projects.

title: Targeting MSUT2 with small molecules to ameliorate pathological tau
text:
Narrative Statement
To date, few clinical trials for AD and related tauopathies have specifically targeted pathological tau, yet
neurofibrillary tangles are the diagnostic neuropathological hallmark of AD and other tauopathies most closely
associated with cognitive decline. To help fill this gap, we propose to develop a novel neuroprotective strategy
that targets pathological tau in AD and related dementias. Specifically, we propose to develop and optimize
small molecule inhibitors of MSUT2 binding to poly(A) RNA. These novel tool compounds will be used to provide
a proof-of-concept demonstration that inhibiting MSUT2 can slow or reverse pathological tau deposition, and
they will support mechanistic investigation of MSUT2 as a critical modulator of pathological tau.

title: Fast and Robust Distortion-Free Diffusion Weighted MRI for the Prostate
text:
Research Narrative
Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) plays a central role in pelvic imaging and prostate cancer diagnosis, but its
clinical utility is hindered by geometric distortion, low resolution, and long scan times. This project aims to
overcome these limitations by developing a distortion-free, high-resolution DWI framework using rapid
acquisition and advanced reconstruction, enabling reliable imaging and quantitative diffusion modeling.
Ultimately, this approach will improve the quality of pelvic imaging, promote early cancer detection, support
precision diagnostics, facilitate the clinical investigation of quantitative prognostic biomarker, and broaden the
utility of prostate MRI.

title: Training OPportunites in Translational Imaging Education and Research (TOP-TIER)
text:
An interdisciplinary approach is required to better prepare future clinician scientists for the challenges and
opportunities of imaging research in Precision Medicine. The TOP-TIER T32 program trains post-doctoral
clinician scientists in the performance of translational imaging research, providing them with the skill set to
transition to independent investigators capable of taking imaging research from bench-to-bedside and
imaging innovation into tomorrow’s healthcare.

title: GENETIC HETEROGENEITY AMONG HUMAN SOMATIC CELLS AND ITS ACCUMULATION WITH AGE
text:
Somatic cell genetic heterogeneity within an individual arises over the course of the human lifespan.
Our human colon crypt whole genome sequencing (WGS) study is the first to quantitatively and qualitatively
measure this cell-to-cell change with age. Building on the work developed during the last 4-year funding cycle,
we propose to establish an accurate rate of somatic mutation accumulation with age and to develop a new
platform that enables easier and non-invasive collection of human tissue samples for measuring human aging.

title: Mechanisms of Gene Regulation During Asymmetric Stem Cell Division
text:
Proposed project investigates how DNA regions of key genes inherited from the mother and father
interact with each other to regulate gene expression in stem cells. This mechanism can help stem
cells to continuously produce mature cells in the tissue. Disruption of such process causes
multiple human diseases, including cancer and tissue degeneration, and our findings will
contribute to understanding these pathologies.

title: Role of the SWI/SNF complex in tumor suppression
text:
Genes encoding SWI/SNF complex subunits are mutated in over 20% of all human cancers, including the
devastating childhood Rhabdoid Tumor. We have identified a gene that, when deleted, specifically kills rhabdoid
cells. The proposed studies are designed to determine the normal function of this gene and the mechanisms by
which its loss kills these cancers and, secondly, to explore novel approaches to circumvent therapeutic
resistance in these aggressive cancers.

title: Ultra-Precise Surgical Navigation With Continuous Anatomy Updates Via Robotically Assisted Endoscopic Computer Vision
text:
We propose to develop an integrated robotic platform for endoscopic image-guided surgery that
will 1) dramatically increase the precision of surgical navigation technology to sub-millimeter
accuracy and 2) permit precise real-time imaging and reconstruction of evolving surgical
anatomy. This game-changing improvement in surgical navigation performance relies on the
realization that motion encodings from a precisely calibrated robotic endoscope holder can
resolve uncertainties in statistical computer vision algorithms to provide precise, adequately
scaled, and re-localized 3D reconstructions of patient anatomy from endoscopic video. This
approach offers significant clinical benefits, including eliminating a major surgical decision fault
mode that leads to patient harm and the ability to continuously maintain correspondence
between the surgical field and anatomic surgical model without intraoperative computed
tomographic scanning.

title: Harnessing TNFa Signaling To Improve Therapeutic Response In Pancreatic Cancer
text:
We found that targeting the oncogenic KRAS-MAPK pathway in pancreatic cancer cells leads to marked
induction of TNF secretion, which drives both death and survival including autophagy. Selective inhibition of
MK2, which controls the survival signaling, aggravates TNF-mediated tumor cell death. On this basis, we will
investigate the mechanisms by which MK2 signaling controls cell survival in cancer cells and shapes the
surrounding fibroblasts and immune cells, with the overarching goal of developing novel therapeutic strategies
that can be advanced into the clinic.

title: Molecular mechanisms underlying endothelial von Willebrand factor exocytosis
text:
von Willebrand factor (vWF) is a blood protein that is required for normal blood coagulation. von Willebrand
disease, caused by deficiency of vWF, is the most common inherited bleeding disorder, while high levels of
vWF in the blood can raise the risk of heart and blood-vessel problems such as heart attacks and strokes. We
will study how cells lining blood vessels release vWF by identifying the key proteins that control this process,
with the goal of developing new treatments to raise vWF when it’s too low or lower it when it’s too high.

title: Network modulation to improve gene therapy in CLN3 disease
text:
In two-thirds of lysosomal storage disorders (LSD), patients suffer neurologic symptoms that are not corrected
by most therapies, including gene replacement, especially if treatment is given after symptom onset. We
recently identified pathologic changes in hippocampal network dynamics that arise early in CLN3 disease, a
representative LSD, and the most common cause of pediatric dementia. The goal of this project is to
understand if early, progressive changes in network physiology in CLN3 disease will establish a point beyond
which gene therapy cannot restore function to a diseased neuronal circuit and to explore if modulating network
activity can modify the efficacy of gene replacement.

title: Endothelial oxygen sensing and metabolic reprogramming in AKI to CKD transition
text:
Currently, there are no effective therapies to promote kidney repair following acute kidney injury.
Consequently, many patients develop chronic kidney disease and other long-term risks including
cardiovascular events and reduced quality of life. By investigating the mechanistic basis and
therapeutic potential of endothelial hypoxia-induced glycolysis/MCT4 axis in post-ischemic kidney
repair, our studies will stimulate new areas for experimental therapeutics in AKI.

title: Developing programmable RNA writing tools with the novel RNA-guided RNA-targeting CRISPR effector Cas7-11
text:
Programmable nucleic acid targeting tools such as CRISPR provide a new modality for
programmable RNA targeting but current RNA-targeting tools suffer from potential issues with
safety, specificity, and versatility. We propose to develop new, specific RNA-targeting CRISPR
systems without off-target collateral activity in cells and engineer these systems to generate
new RNA writing technologies capable of all possible base conversions, insertions or deletions
of any size, and exon replacement. The technologies developed from this work will accelerate
the study and modeling of disease biology and provide a revolutionary platform for RNA-based
therapeutics, including many triplet repeat disorders.

title: Platelet-derived FVIII Gene Therapy of Hemophilia A
text:
Hemophilia A is a bleeding disorder resulting from factor VIII (FVIII) deficiency. The development of inhibitory
antibodies against FVIII is not only a severe and important complication of protein replacement therapy, but
also a major concern in gene therapy of hemophilia A. In this project, we will develop a novel approach by
targeting the synthesis of FVIII to blood platelets to provide therapeutic protein and induce immune tolerance in
hemophilia A even in the presence of inhibitory antibodies.
